topics.name: Fertility & Birth
topics.blurb: Powers over conception, childbirth and the increase of families and herds - appealed to more often, and by more people, than the sky gods.

topics.name: Kingship & Justice
topics.blurb: Divine authority and the law it underwrites - the gods a ruler claimed descent from, and the ones who judged the ruler.

topics.name: Agriculture & Harvest
topics.blurb: The gods standing behind the farming year - planting, rain on the crop, the grain in the store, and the prosperity that follows a good one.

topics.name: Creation & Origins
topics.blurb: The first powers - those who made the world, or were the world before anything was made of it.

topics.name: Magic & Prophecy
topics.blurb: Those who see what has not happened yet, and those who change what has.

topics.name: Protection & Guardianship
topics.blurb: Warders of doors, roads, households and children - the everyday gods, appealed to most often.

topics.name: Death & the Underworld
topics.blurb: Rulers and wardens of the land of the dead, judges of souls, and the guides who carry the newly dead across.

topics.name: Earth & Wilderness
topics.blurb: The ground itself, the mountains standing on it, and the wild country beyond the last field.

topics.name: Sea & Waters
topics.blurb: Ocean powers, river spirits and the gods sailors bargained with.

topics.name: Sun, Moon & Stars
topics.blurb: The lights that keep time - solar and lunar deities, dawn-bringers, and the powers behind the constellations.

topics.name: War & Battle
topics.blurb: Gods who decide the outcome of fighting - patrons of armies, personifications of the battle rage, and the powers soldiers prayed to before a line advanced.

topics.name: Sky, Storm & Thunder
topics.blurb: Thunderers and sky-fathers: the weather as an expression of divine temper.

topics.name: Wisdom & Knowledge
topics.blurb: Patrons of writing, counsel and memory - the gods invoked before a difficult decision rather than a difficult journey.

topics.name: Healing & Medicine
topics.blurb: Physicians among the gods - and the same powers, often, that sent the disease.

topics.name: Love & Desire
topics.blurb: Powers of attraction, marriage and longing - and of the trouble that follows them.

topics.name: Craft & Fire
topics.blurb: Smiths, makers and the fire they work with - the gods of everything built rather than grown.

topics.name: Tricksters & Chaos
topics.blurb: The gods who break the rules the other gods depend on - and are tolerated because the world would seize up without them.
